text:
### Observed differences

- Routing into the A04–A05 branch increased. In the earlier window, A09 — which appears in about 66 in 100 traces in both windows — sent about 55 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A03 and only about 7 in 100 to A05; in the later window it sent about 43 in 100 to A03, about 20 in 100 to A04 and about 16 in 100 to A05. [DIR007, OCC008]
- A04's own outgoing mix moved the same way: transitions to A05 rose from about 17 to about 31 in 100, while transitions to A02 fell from about 30 to 17 and to A08 from about 18 to 12 in 100. [DIR003]
- A05 was executed in more cases: it appeared in about 26 in 100 traces before versus about 37 in 100 after (mean occurrences per trace 0.39 → 0.58, with roughly 1.5 occurrences per trace containing it in both windows, so the increase comes from more traces, not more repetitions). A04 and A06 each rose from about 28 to about 34 in 100 traces. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- A02 and A10 largely exchanged their preferred successors: earlier A02 sent about 58 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A10 and about 35 to A07, while A10 sent about 60 to A07 and about 35 to A02; in the later window A02 sends about 58 to A07 and 39 to A10, and A10 sends about 50 to A02 and 38 to A07. The rare A02→A04 transition (about 4 in 100 earlier) was not observed later. [DIR002, DIR008]
- A01 and A11 occurred slightly more often and repeated more often: participation about 65 → 69 in 100 traces, mean occurrences 0.88 → 1.06, recurrence support about 0.19 → 0.26; their outgoing distributions changed only marginally. [OCC001, OCC010, DIR001, DIR009]
- Smaller outgoing redistributions at A05, A06 and A07 (for example A06→A01 rising from about 2 to 9 in 100) have only moderate empirical strength (about 67 in 100 reference comparisons smaller) and may be sampling variation. [DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, existing alternative paths are taken with different frequencies, with clearly more case flow through the A04–A05 part of the process: A09 routed relatively more of its transitions to A04 and A05 (together about 20 → 36 in 100) and less to A03; A04 passed more of its traffic on to A05 (about 17 → 31 in 100) and less to A02 and A08; and A05 ran in about 37 in 100 traces versus about 26 in 100 before. Every activity and transition involved remains well observed in both windows, so this reads as a shift between existing alternatives rather than paths being added, removed or bypassed. The routing changes are observed directly at two source activities and are about as large as or larger than roughly 99 in 100 random re-splits, and the participation increases at A04, A05 and A06 point in the same direction. [DIR003, DIR007, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]

Limitations: the evidence file contains no screening baseline, so the number of qualifying items cannot be compared against a chance expectation; the routing and participation items can be two faces of the same rerouted traces and are not independent confirmations; and several activities show literally identical profiles (A02/A07/A10, A08/A09, A01/A11), so items within these groups duplicate one another. The main competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is correlated sampling fluctuation between the two 200-trace windows, particularly for the moderate-strength redistributions at A05, A06 and A07. [DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, OCC001, OCC002, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]

Other differences: A02 and A10 largely exchanged their preferred successors (A02: to A10 about 58 → 39 in 100, to A07 about 35 → 58; A10: to A07 about 60 → 38, to A02 about 35 → 50) — the evidence shows only these successor shares, not the positions of the activities; and A01 and A11 occur and repeat somewhat more often (recurrence support about 0.19 → 0.26). [DIR002, DIR008, OCC001, OCC010]
